articles.title: Olympic hero Alysa Liu to sit out figure skating season before 2027 return
articles.summary: US star plans to return for 2027-28 season. Liu will continue training during year away. Skater says break ‘makes the most sense’ Olympic champion Alysa Liu will sit out the 2026-27 figure skating season, taking another break from competition while continuing to train ahead of a planned return the…
body: The 21-year-old American announced her decision on social media, saying she wanted time to “recalibrate” and develop her skating away from the demands of competition.
“I always want to challenge myself in new ways, so my artistry and skating can evolve,” Liu wrote. “It’s important to me that my sport reflects my personal growth.”

Liu told NBC Sports that she intends to continue working with her longtime Bay Area coaches, Phillip DiGuglielmo and Massimo Scali, with an emphasis on her “overall artistry, spins, jumps, everything”.
“I really want to improve my skating, and I wanted to take the time to do that for myself and just to evolve,” she said. “And then I’ll be back after that is done.”

articles.title: ‘Icon of our game’: All-Australian selection lifts ruck great Max Gawn into rarified air
articles.summary: Melbourne player awarded record-breaking ninth blazer. AFL minor premiers Fremantle lead league with five selections. Melbourne colossus Max Gawn has underlined his status as the greatest ruckman of the modern era, awarded an unprecedented ninth All-Australian blazer after another brilliant…
body: Gawn was named captain of the representative side, which also featured Demons teammate Kysaiah Pickett among a record five Indigenous players chosen.
Minor premiers Fremantle led the league with five selections, headlined by key forward Josh Treacy, one of nine players named for the first time.
Gawn’s record-breaking ninth selection comes after the 34-year-old champion defied changes to ruck rules to maintain his status as the competition’s dominant ruckman.

Gawn’s latest inclusion pushed him clear of fellow greats Gary Ablett Snr, Gary Ablett Jnr, Patrick Dangerfield, Lance Franklin, Robert Harvey, and Mark Ricciuto, who all have eight blazers. That group was joined by Western Bulldogs skipper Marcus Bontempelli.

articles.title: Alcaraz and Williams thrill in brief but bright US Open mixed doubles showing
articles.summary: Serena Williams and Carlos Alcaraz were among the star double-acts in New York as the US Open mixed doubles competition got under way on Tuesday.
body: That was how Carlos Alcaraz settled back into competitive action at the US Open, partnering the American great as she returned to her home slam after a four-year absence.
The tournament's revamped mixed doubles format has attracted criticism for favouring the allure of the sport's top singles stars at the expense of established doubles players.
But the crowds turned out and produced a terrific atmosphere for the tournament's headline act, with about 15,000 people packed inside Arthur Ashe Stadium.
All four doubles specialist pairings lost to a team of singles players on Tuesday, while Alcaraz and Williams fell in the quarter-finals.

articles.title: Serena Williams thrills New York crowd on US Open return with Alcaraz
articles.summary: Former women’s No 1 proves she’s no nostalgia act before star pairing crash out in mixed doubles quarter-finals. Serena Williams’ US Open return lasted two matches and one afternoon Tuesday as she and Carlos Alcaraz followed a first-round win with a quarter-final defeat by Belinda Bencic and Flavio…
body: Back inside Arthur Ashe Stadium 1,453 days after the defeat by Ajla Tomljanovic that had appeared to end her career, Williams emerged from the tunnel at half past three to the roars of more than 10,000 spectators. As the 44-year-old American and Alcaraz warmed up in matching purple-and-black Nike kits, public-address announcer Andy Taylor rattled off her accolades one by one to a steadily rising wall of applause. Together they carried 30 grand slam singles titles, a record for a mixed-doubles team at a major.

The tournament was still officially in qualifying week, but the crowds had already swelled to main-draw proportions. The scenes along the boardwalk from the Mets-Willets Point subway station to the Billie Jean King National Tennis Center looked like the middle weekend of the tournament. The No 7 train exhaled bursts of fans every few minutes. Vendors rolled enormous coolers through the crowd, selling cold water and canned soda. Jehovah’s Witnesses stood beside literature carts.

articles.title: Carabao Cup round-up: Leeds beat Forest again, Brentford hit Birmingham for six
articles.summary: Dan James sets Leeds on way, Nathan Collins doubles up. Peterborough thump Watford 5-1, West Ham win 4-1. Leeds secured a second win at Premier League rivals Nottingham Forest in three days to book a spot in the Carabao Cup third round.
body: Before the weekend, the West Yorkshire club had not won at the City Ground since 1972. After defeat, new Forest manager Oliver Glasner said he is not a “magician”.

“Right now, we are far away from where we want to be,” Glasner said. “The fact is that this team had a relegation battle for nine months. Very turbulent season and it ended with a huge effort to stay in the league, and this is our starting point.

“It’s really very important not to blame anybody because sometimes I tell them facts and they say, ‘Oh, Glasner is complaining’. No, no, no. But then maybe your best midfielder [Elliot Anderson] leaves the club and now we expect we compete for European places because Oliver Glasner is in. Sorry, this is what I can’t deliver within six weeks. I’m no magician, no messiah, just hard work. That is what we have to do.”

Callum Wilson scored just six minutes into his full debut and captain Nathan Collins headed home twice as Brentford hammered Birmingham 6-1 at St Andrew’s. Aaron Hickey, Mikkel Damsgaard and Igor Thiago were also on target for the Bees after Demarai Gray briefly cancelled out Wilson’s opener.

articles.title: Cardiff's Anyadike, 15, sets new EFL Cup record as youngest player
articles.summary: Cardiff City's Noah Anyadike, 15, becomes the youngest player in EFL Cup history after starting their second-round defeat against Norwich City.
body: The Bluebirds had just completed their second season at the Cardiff City Stadium when the youngster was born - and that is where he made his debut 15 years later.
Without a senior option at centre-back due to an injury crisis, Wales youth international Anyadike was handed his debut at 15 years and 98 days old.
His inclusion from the start saw him break the record previously held by Harvey Elliot, who featured in 2018 for Fulham against Millwall aged 15 years and 174 days.
But in a cruel twist of fate, Anyadike, who also became the youngest player in Cardiff history, hobbled off with a muscle cramp in the second half.

articles.title: Bruno Fernandes and Khadija Shaw win PFA Player of the Year awards
articles.summary: Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes has been crowned Professional Footballers' Association Player of the Year as Manchester City's Khadija Shaw won the women's award for the second time.
body: Playmaker Fernandes broke the all-time record for Premier League assists during an outstanding 2025-26 campaign, setting up 21 goals as he surpassed Thierry Henry and Kevin De Bruyne.
The 31-year-old also scored nine times as United overcome a shaky first half of the campaign to finish third in the Premier League under Michael Carrick and earn a Champions League return.
Fernandes was pleased to have been voted the winner by his fellow professionals.
He said: "It is obviously a very proud moment. They are the ones you go on the pitch against and it's probably not easy to vote for someone you play against, so it is a very good moment."

articles.title: Fernandes and Shaw win PFA player of the year awards
articles.summary: Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes and Manchester City forward Khadija Shaw win the Professional Footballers' Associations men's and women's player of the year awards.
body: Both were previously named the Football Writers' Association men's and women's footballers of the year for the 2025-26 season.
Fernandes, who last season broke the record for the most assists in a single Premier League campaign with 21, is the first United player to win the award since Wayne Rooney in 2010.
It is a second win in three seasons for Shaw, who secured her third consecutive Women's Super League (WSL) golden boot with 21 goals as Man City were crowned champions.
City defender Nico O'Reilly succeeds Morgan Rogers as men's young player of the year, with the versatile 21-year-old cementing his place in the starting XI.

articles.title: Williams and Alcaraz reach mixed doubles quarters before exit
articles.summary: Star pairing Serena Williams and Carlos Alcaraz reached the quarter-finals of the US Open mixed doubles before being beaten by fourth seeds Belinda Bencic and Flavio Cobolli.
body: Williams - a 23-time Grand Slam singles champion - returned to tennis in June at the age of 44 and secured her first professional win since 2022 as she and Alcaraz beat Britain's Lloyd Glasspool and partner Erin Routliffe in their opening match.

It was also seven-time major winner Alcaraz's first match back on tour after a wrist injury sidelined the reigning men's singles champion since April. The 22-year-old was born five years after Williams won the 1998 mixed doubles title at Flushing Meadows.
The dynamic pairing bounced back from a slow start to claim a 5-3 4-1 opening victory over Routliffe and Glasspool, much to the delight of fans inside Arthur Ashe Stadium.
"I never expected to be back on this court," Williams said. "I never thought this would happen."

articles.title: Springfield Cardinals getting new name, logos and uniforms in 2027
articles.summary: SPRINGFIELD, Mo. — The Springfield Cardinals will soon have a new name. The organization announced Tuesday that it will rebrand following the 2026 Minor League Baseball season, ending more than two decades under the Springfield Cardinals name.
body: Beginning in 2026, the team will have a new name, logos and uniforms. The franchise will remain in Springfield, continue playing at Route 66 Stadium and remain the Double-A affiliate of the St. Louis Cardinals.
The new identity has already been selected, according to the team, but fans will have to wait a little longer to find out what it is.
The organization plans to unveil the new name, logos and uniforms during a free launch party at Route 66 Stadium on Tuesday, Oct. 6. Additional details will be announced later.
The Springfield Cardinals have played in the city since 2005. The organization said the change intended to give the team an identity more closely connected to Springfield and southwest Missouri.

articles.title: All Blacks need late surge to avoid shock defeat to Lions
articles.summary: New Zealand fought back from an 18-point ‌deficit in the second half to beat the Lions 41-35 and avoid a shock defeat at Ellis Park on Tuesday.
body: It means that the All Blacks have swept all four provincial teams to remain undefeated on their six-week, eight-match tour of South Africa, on top of beating the Springboks 33-16 in ​the first Test at the weekend.

New Zealand fielded only three players from that Saturday Test victory over South Africa on the same ground and involved five injury replacements summoned on tour - including one who arrived on Monday - as well as giving a debut to prop Saula Ma'u.
Their defence struggled and missed 19 tackles over the course of the contest that saw them trail 14-0 after seven minutes.

They were still behind at half-time and 35-17 behind in the 47th minute, as the Lions threatened to become the first South African provincial side to beat New Zealand since Orange Free State, now known as the Cheetahs, in 1976.

articles.title: Wilson scores on full debut as Brentford hit Birmingham for six
articles.summary: Callum Wilson scored just six minutes into his full debut and captain Nathan Collins converted two headers as Brentford routed Championship side Birmingham 6-1.
body: The 34-year-old Wilson, who joined on a free transfer from relegated West Ham, seized his first opportunity with a crisp finish which took a deflection off defender Dael Fry, who had a debut to forget.
Brentford's Premier League quality was evident throughout and although Blues equalised through Demarai Gray just before the half-hour they were level for just seven minutes.
Lax defending saw Aaron Hickey and Collins score in quick succession to effectively seal the tie before half-time, with Mikkel Damsgaard getting on the end of a counter-attack to add the fourth.
Igor Thiago's smart close-range finish sent fans streaming for the exit, missing Collins' second header.
